ai.title: Add /chats command for CLI chat history
ai.summary: New /chats command opens a searchable chat history screen in the CLI. Users can browse, search, and resume past conversations directly from the terminal. The feature adds a new ChatHistoryScreen component, a zustand store for state management, and utility functions to scan the local chats directory. Two-phase loading ensures fast initial render while backgrounding the rest of the history.

eli5.text: When you are using the CLI chat, you can now type /chats (or /history) to open a screen that shows your past conversations. From that screen, you can browse or search your chat history and pick a previous conversation to jump back into. The feature loads the most recent 25 chats immediately so the list appears fast, then continues scanning up to 1,000 total chats in the background for thorough searching and resuming. This is live today in CLI version 1.0.577 as a built-in command, no flags or extra setup needed.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.577 release
ai.summary: CLI release version bumped from 1.0.576 to 1.0.577 in cli/release/package.json. This release bundles the previously committed /chats slash command for searchable CLI chat history and the reordering of the slash command list and help banner shortcuts. No functional command logic changes were introduced in this bump commit itself.
ai.evidence: Modified file cli/release/package.json; version field changed from "1.0.576" to "1.0.577"

eli5.text: You can now look up and jump back into your past conversations directly from the terminal. A new chat-history browser lets you search through earlier chats and resume them without leaving the command line, and it loads quickly first while pulling in the rest of your history in the background. The list of built-in slash commands shown in the help screen has also been tidied up, so the most useful actions like connecting to Claude and running the setup wizard now appear at the top, while account and ad-toggle commands are grouped toward the bottom. Upgrading gives you faster access to the commands you use most and a simple way to rediscover or return to any previous conversation right from your terminal.

ai.title: Send last user and assistant message for ads endpoint
ai.summary: Gravity ad request payload changed from last 3 user messages to last 1 user and last 1 assistant message. Added `sessionId` from `loggerContext` to request body. Scope: `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts`.

eli5.text: When the app asks its ad service for a relevant advertisement, it now sends just the most recent message you typed plus the assistant's most recent reply, instead of the last three messages you sent. It also includes a session identifier so the ad service can track the conversation. This makes the ad request lighter and helps the service understand the immediate context of your chat.

eli5.text: If you use the command-line tools built from this code repository, you may now see agents moved into a dedicated folder called 'agents' that the tools bundle directly, while the original spot is now used only for agents specific to this repository. You won't see a difference in commands you run, but the developers can now better organize which agents ship with the tool versus which stay local. This change is already in place and affects how agent code is structured behind the scenes.

ai.title: CLI auto-spawns user agents for base agents
ai.summary: Base agents now automatically include user-defined agents in their spawnableAgents list. This removes the need to manually update base agent definitions. Implemented in local-agent-registry.ts by appending user agent IDs to base agent configs. Agent runtime main-prompt.ts no longer overrides spawnableAgents with template-only lists.

eli5.text: When you write a custom agent and tell the system about it, that agent now automatically shows up as something any of the ready-made "base" assistants can hand off to, without you having to go edit those base assistants yourself. The system gathers your custom agent IDs and tacks them onto the list of assistants each base agent is allowed to spawn, so your new helper is reachable right away. If you look at a base agent's settings, you will see your custom agents quietly added to its spawnable list; if you did not define any custom agents, nothing about the base agents changes.

ai.title: Remove extraneous agents build artifacts
ai.summary: Deleted generated JavaScript files in `agents/.agents/` (constants, types). These were compiled artifacts from `.ts` sources, not source code. Cleanup reduces repository size and prevents stale build outputs from being committed.

eli5.text: The development team cleaned up a folder in their project that contained duplicate, automatically-generated files. These files were copies of other files and served no purpose, so they were deleted. This cleanup helps keep the project organized and prevents confusion from stale files that might otherwise be accidentally used or edited. The project itself works exactly the same as before.

eli5.text: When you send a request through the ads endpoint, it can now receive an optional session identifier alongside the conversation messages. The system passes that identifier along to Gravity whenever it exists, so the upstream request includes both your user id and the relevant session. If you never include a session id, nothing changes; the payload stays exactly as it was.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.578 release
ai.summary: Version `1.0.578` bumps the CLI package manifest in `cli/release/package.json` from `1.0.577`, packaging the day's earlier CLI work. This release ships the new `/chats` slash command for browsing and resuming chat history from the terminal, the shift to box-drawing Unicode table rendering in the markdown renderer, the Gravity ad request payload change to send one user and one assistant message plus an optional `sessionId`, and the agent directory restructure that moved bundled `.agents` under `agents/` and made base agents auto-spawn user-defined agents. No functional code changed in this commit itself; it purely tags the accumulated CLI changes.
ai.evidence: Commit 1c7ec551 modifies `cli/release/package.json`, bumping the `version` field from `1.0.577` to `1.0.578`. No other files changed in this release-bump commit.

eli5.text: This release makes Freebuff smarter at working with custom AI helpers you bring to your projects. It now automatically includes your own custom agents whenever you ask a built-in helper to call on another agent, so you spend less time wiring things up by hand. The advertising suggestions shown to you get better because they now look at your most recent conversation turn plus the assistant's reply, instead of just a longer chat history, making the suggestions more relevant and timely. The system also tracks your current session so ads can be personalized to what you're actively working on without losing privacy. Upgrading gives you smoother, more automatic collaboration between built-in and custom agents, plus more useful and context-aware ad placements that adapt to your current session.

ai.title: CLI markdown tables use box-drawing characters
ai.summary: CLI `markdown-renderer` replaces pipe-delimited output with Unicode box-drawing characters (┌, ─, │) for table borders. New `truncateText` and `padText` helpers ensure column alignment using `stringWidth` for accurate Unicode width calculation. Logic adjusts column widths proportionally to fit within `codeBlockWidth`, adding ellipsis to overflowed cells. Affects `cli/src/utils/markdown-renderer.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you run a tool in the command line that outputs a table, rows and columns now draw themselves with clean box-drawing lines (like the edges of a text message bubble) instead of plain dashes and pipes. Any cell whose content is too long gets cut off with an ellipsis, and the remaining space is filled with subtle padding so everything lines up neatly even when columns have to be squeezed to fit your terminal width. You'd notice that tables look tidier and stay aligned regardless of how narrow your window is, and no part of a row ever spills over into the next line.
